name: layout-shells
summary: The 4 route shells (chosen by the src/app.vue switcher + route.meta.layout override) + 2 content layouts that render inside Layout. They differ by chrome: Layout (nav + header + content, the default) · LoginLayout (bare sign-in) · EmptyLayout / PublicLayout (no chrome, padded) · MonitorHierarchyLayout (tree + content) · Settings two-pane (menu + content).
decisionFlow: Pick the SHELL = the page's top-level skeleton once you know the screen type: list-with-detail, full-page form/record, dashboard canvas, or a centered auth/empty layout.
High-complexity record you must deep-link to / keep in browser history? -> full-page shell (route), NOT a drawer or modal.
Editing a row while keeping the list visible behind? -> keep the list shell + open a drawer (see drawer.json), don't navigate to a new shell.
A quick confirm / small focused task? -> stay on the current shell + modal (see modal.json). Reserve a new shell/route for a whole screen, not an overlay.
do: Use Layout for in-app pages (default — no route override).
Use LoginLayout for auth screens; it's also the not-logged-in fallback.
MonitorHierarchyLayout / Settings two-pane render INSIDE Layout — they are content layouts, not route shells.
dont: Don't treat MonitorHierarchyLayout as a route shell (0 meta.layout overrides).
Don't add a route layout override unless you need EmptyLayout / PublicLayout.

a11y.summary: Shell chrome reference. Each shell wraps the routed page; landmarks + focus order follow the App shell. LoginLayout is a bare, focus-trapped auth screen.

knownIssues: MonitorHierarchyLayout is a content layout, NOT a route shell (0 meta.layout overrides) — a common misclassification.

[element] The obs-layout-* WEB COMPONENT is a fixed visual demo, not a slotted layout primitive — you can't put a real page inside it. Use the layout GUIDANCE (decisionFlow/regions) + compose the shell from atoms + the 12-col grid + tokens.
changelog: 2026-06-29: added — the 4 route shells + 2 content layouts, with a recognizable per-shell preview.
whenToUse: Which page frame to use — almost always the default Layout; switch only for login, print/export, or system (upgrade/restore) pages.
usedIn: LoginLayout — login / reset / forgot + disk-full + the unauth fallback.
EmptyLayout — print-safe report export · PublicLayout — upgrade / restore.
MonitorHierarchyLayout — log / inventory / topology (inside Layout) · Settings two-pane — all settings submodules.
